original_test_run.cause: duplicate original question row counted once when rejecting unique duplicate key; preserved and preregistered narrow fix

execution.external_real_data_execution: Code blob fetched directly from own GitHub, dynamically evaluated in connector orchestration with the same function body; identical SHA1 Git blob verified; original question and resolution JSON read-only from pinned public original GitHub upstream commit; no original files copied to user repo.
execution.original_license: CC BY-SA 4.0 per original README and LICENSE; source attribution and non-person aggregate counts only

important_limits: Nonprobability sources acled, FRED, DBnomics, Wikipedia and yfinance contain raw predictions in units other than probabilities; 250 per cohort were semantically excluded even when numeric values could appear inside [0,1].
This is real original benchmark public question/outcome data, not a study of participation, PFL users, random assignment or human treatment effects.
Official original data may include market-generated aggregate probabilities but not individual forecast rows; aggregate probability not a participant-level privacy inference.
0.5 Brier comparison is a diagnostic sanity comparator, deliberately not a competent predictive rival, so zero claims of performance advantage or causal novelty.

The 60 accepted questions are an outcome-selected resolved subset (52+8), not representative of every question or the full market; some sources have repeated time-series resolution per id and fail closed.

Date-order requires question freeze before due before resolution date, but original resolution_date precision is only day-level and questions may have market-specific close dates; no event-level PFL exposure can be inferred.
CC BY-SA terms and external platforms' attribution/rights for underlying question text must be revisited before product republication; we did not copy text or create a public product.
This result is an engineering data validation advance that makes future evaluation safer; not a novel scientific mechanism or causal test.
